Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 40, verses 1–3:

Tafsir of Surah Ghafir [in some manuscripts: "al-Mu'min"].

It is a Meccan surah.

Some of the early scholars (al-salaf) disliked saying "al-Hawamim" (the Hawamim), among them Muhammad ibn Sirin, and said instead "Al Ha-Mim" (the family of Ha-Mim).

ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud said: "Al Ha-Mim" is the brocade (dibaj) of the Qur'an.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: Everything has a core (lubab), and the core of the Qur'an is "Al Ha-Mim", or he said: the Hawamim.

Mis'ar ibn Kidam said: They used to call them "the brides" (al-ʿaraʾis).

The eminent imam Abu ʿUbayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated all of this in his book "Fada'il al-Qur'an" (Virtues of the Qur'an) (pp. 137, 138). Humayd ibn Zanjawayh said: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, Israʾil narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿUbayd Allah, who said: The likeness of the Qur'an is like the likeness of a man who set out to seek a dwelling for his family. He passed by the trace of rain, and while he was walking through it and marveling at it, he descended upon soft, level gardens, and said: "I was amazed at the first rain, but this is even more amazing, and more amazing!" It was said to him: "The likeness of the first rain is the likeness of the greatness of the Qur'an, and the likeness of these soft, level gardens is the likeness of Al Ha-Mim in the Qur'an." Al-Baghawi cited it.

Ibn Lahi'ah narrated from Yazid ibn Abi Habib: that al-Jarrah ibn Abi al-Jirah narrated to him from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Everything has a core, and the core of the Qur'an is the Hawamim." (Narrated by Abu ʿUbayd in Fada'il al-Qur'an (p. 137) and al-Baghawi in his tafsir (7/134).)

Ibn Masʿud said: "When I come upon Al Ha-Mim, I have come upon gardens in which I delight."

Abu ʿUbayd said: al-Ashja'i narrated to us, Mis'ar (i.e., Ibn Kidam) narrated to us, from someone who narrated to him: that a man saw Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him) building a mosque, and asked him: "What is this?" He said: "I am building it for the sake of Al Ha-Mim." (Fada'il al-Qur'an of Abu ʿUbayd (p. 137).)

It may be that this mosque which Abu al-Darda' built is the one attributed to him inside the citadel of Damascus. And its preservation and safeguarding may be by the blessing of his [recitation] and the blessing of what was prescribed for it, for this phrase indicates victory over enemies, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his companions in some of the battles: "If you spend the night [on an attack], then say: Ha-Mim, they will not be helped" and in another narration: "they will not be helped."

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ahmad ibn al-Hakam ibn Zabyan ibn Khalaf al-Mazini and Muhammad ibn al-Layth al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Masʿud narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Mulaiki narrated to us, from Zurarah ibn Mus'ab, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi) and the beginning of Ha-Mim al-Mu'min, will be protected that day from every evil."

Then he said: We do not know it to be narrated except through this chain. And al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of al-Mulaiki, and said: some of the people of knowledge spoke about it because of his memorization. (Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2879.)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

As for the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah), it was mentioned at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, sufficient so that it need not be repeated here.

It has been said that "Ha-Mim" is one of the names of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and they recited in support of this:

It reminds me of Ha-Mim, while the spear is trembling... so why did he not recite Ha-Mim before the advance...

It has been reported in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Muhallab ibn Abi Sufrah, who said: someone who heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say told me: "If you spend the night [on an attack], then say: Ha-Mim, they will not be helped." This is a sahih chain. (Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2597; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1682.)

Abu ʿUbayd chose to narrate it as: "then say: Ha-Mim, they will not be helped" (lā yunṣarū), meaning: if you say that, they will not be helped, taking it as the response (jaza') to his saying "then say."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The revelation of the Book from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾, meaning: the sending down of this Book, which is the Qur'an, is from Allah, the Possessor of might and knowledge, so His presence cannot be approached, and nothing is hidden from Him, even if His veils are thick.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance﴾, meaning: He forgives the sins that have passed, and accepts repentance in the future from whoever turns to Him and submits before Him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Severe in punishment﴾, meaning: for whoever rebels, transgresses, prefers the worldly life, defies Allah's commands, and oppresses. In this verse hope and fear are combined. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ [al-Hijr: 49–50]. He often pairs these two attributes in many places in the Qur'an, so that the servant remains between hope and fear.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Possessor of bounty﴾, Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means abundance and wealth. Likewise said Mujahid and Qatadah.

Yazid ibn al-Asamm said: ﴿Possessor of bounty﴾ means abundant good.

ʿIkrimah said: ﴿Possessor of bounty﴾ means possessor of favor (al-mann).

Qatadah said: it means possessor of blessings and bounties.

The meaning is that He is the One who bestows grace upon His servants, favoring them with what they have of benefactions and gifts, the thanks for one of which they cannot fulfill: ﴿If you tried to count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾ [Ibrahim: 34].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾, meaning: He has no equal in all His attributes, so there is no deity other than Him and no lord besides Him. ﴿To Him is the destination﴾, meaning: the return and the place of return, so He recompenses every doer for his deed. ﴿And He is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41].

Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash said: I heard Abu Ishaq al-Sabiʿi say: A man came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, I have killed someone; is there repentance for me?" ʿUmar recited to him: ﴿Ha-Mim. The revelation of the Book from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing. Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance, severe in punishment﴾ and said: "Act, and do not despair."

Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, the wording is his, and Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Marwan al-Raqqi narrated to us, ʿUmar (i.e., Ibn Ayyub) narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Barqan informed us, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, who said: There was a man from the people of Syria, a strong man, who used to visit ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him). ʿUmar missed him and said: "What has become of so-and-so son of so-and-so?" They said: "O Commander of the Faithful, he persists in this drinking." He said: So ʿUmar called his scribe and said: "Write: From ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab to so-and-so son of so-and-so, peace be upon you. I praise Allah to you, besides whom there is no deity, Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment, Possessor of bounty; there is no deity except Him, to Him is the destination." Then he said to his companions: "Pray to Allah for your brother that He turn his heart and accept his repentance." When the man received ʿUmar's letter, he began reading it and repeating it, saying: "Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment. He has warned me of His punishment and promised me that He will forgive me."

Abu Nuʿaym also narrated it from the hadith of Ja'far ibn Burqan, adding: "He kept repeating it to himself, then he wept, then he breathed his last and died well. When ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) was informed of his news, he said: 'Thus should you do: when you see your brother slip into a lapse, then support him and guide him, pray to Allah to accept his repentance, and do not be helpers of Satan against him.'" (Hilyat al-Awliya' (4/97).)

Ibn Abi Hatim said: ʿUmar ibn Shabbah narrated to us, Hammad ibn Waqid (Abu ʿUmar al-Saffar) narrated to us, Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, saying: I was with Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr in the outskirts of Kufa. I entered an orchard to pray two rak'ahs, and I began with: ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ of al-Mu'min, until I reached: ﴿There is no deity except Him, to Him is the destination﴾. Then a man behind me on a white mule, wearing Yemeni garments, said: "When you say ﴿Forgiver of sin﴾, say: 'O Forgiver of sin, forgive my sin.' When you say ﴿Accepter of repentance﴾, say: 'O Accepter of repentance, accept my repentance.' And when you say ﴿Severe in punishment﴾, say: 'O Severe in punishment, do not punish me.'" He said: I turned around and saw no one, so I went out to the gate and said: "Has a man in Yemeni garments passed by you?" They said: "We saw no one." They thought that he was Elias (Ilyas).

Then he narrated it through another route from Thabit, with similar wording, and in it there is no mention of Elias.

As for His saying: ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾, meaning: He has no equal in all His attributes, so there is no deity other than Him and no lord besides Him. ﴿To Him is the destination﴾, meaning: the return and the place of return, so He recompenses every doer for his deed. ﴿And He is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41].

Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash said: I heard Abu Ishaq al-Sabiʿi say: A man came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, I have killed someone; is there repentance for me?" ʿUmar recited to him: ﴿Ha-Mim. The revelation of the Book from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing. Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance, severe in punishment﴾ and said: "Act, and do not despair."

Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, the wording is his, and Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Marwan al-Raqqi narrated to us, ʿUmar (i.e., Ibn Ayyub) narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Barqan informed us, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, who said: There was a man from the people of Syria, a strong man, who used to visit ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him). ʿUmar missed him and said: "What has become of so-and-so son of so-and-so?" They said: "O Commander of the Faithful, he persists in this drinking." He said: So ʿUmar called his scribe and said: "Write: From ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab to so-and-so son of so-and-so, peace be upon you. I praise Allah to you, besides whom there is no deity, Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment, Possessor of bounty; there is no deity except Him, to Him is the destination." Then he said to his companions: "Pray to Allah for your brother that He turn his heart and accept his repentance." When the man received ʿUmar's letter, he began reading it and repeating it, saying: "Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment. He has warned me of His punishment and promised me that He will forgive me."

Abu Nuʿaym also narrated it from the hadith of Ja'far ibn Burqan, adding: "He kept repeating it to himself, then he wept, then he breathed his last and died well. When ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) was informed of his news, he said: 'Thus should you do: when you see your brother slip into a lapse, then support him and guide him, pray to Allah to accept his repentance, and do not be helpers of Satan against him.'" (Hilyat al-Awliya' (4/97).)

Ibn Abi Hatim said: ʿUmar ibn Shabbah narrated to us, Hammad ibn Waqid (Abu ʿUmar al-Saffar) narrated to us, Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, saying: I was with Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr in the outskirts of Kufa. I entered an orchard to pray two rak'ahs, and I began with: ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ of al-Mu'min, until I reached: ﴿There is no deity except Him, to Him is the destination﴾. Then a man behind me on a white mule, wearing Yemeni garments, said: "When you say ﴿Forgiver of sin﴾, say: 'O Forgiver of sin, forgive my sin.' When you say ﴿Accepter of repentance﴾, say: 'O Accepter of repentance, accept my repentance.' And when you say ﴿Severe in punishment﴾, say: 'O Severe in punishment, do not punish me.'" He said: I turned around and saw no one, so I went out to the gate and said: "Has a man in Yemeni garments passed by you?" They said: "We saw no one." They thought that he was Elias (Ilyas).

Then he narrated it through another route from Thabit, with similar wording, and in it there is no mention of Elias.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, exalted is He, says: None dispute concerning the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, after the clear proof has come to them and its evidence has become manifest. ﴿Except those who disbelieve﴾, meaning those who deny the verses, proofs and arguments of Allah. ﴿So let not their movement throughout the land deceive you﴾, meaning their wealth, its comforts and its splendour, as He said: ﴿Let not the strutting of those who disbelieve throughout the land deceive you. It is a brief enjoyment; then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 196-197]. And He said: ﴿We grant them enjoyment for a little; then We will compel them to a severe punishment﴾ [Luqman: 24].

Then He said, consoling His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) regarding the denial of his people, that he has in the example of the prophets before him a precedent: their nations denied them and opposed them, and only a few of them believed. He said: ﴿The people of Noah denied before them﴾, and he was the first messenger Allah sent, forbidding the worship of idols. ﴿And the factions after them﴾, meaning from every nation. ﴿And every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him﴾, meaning they were eager to kill him by every possible means, and some of them did kill their messenger. ﴿And they argued with falsehood to refute the truth thereby﴾, meaning they resorted to doubt in order to reject the clear and manifest truth.

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, 'Arim Abu al-Nu'man narrated to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard my father narrate from Hanash, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever helps falsehood in order to refute truth by his falsehood, the protection of Allah and the protection of His Messenger is removed from him."

[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/215). Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (4/100) through the route of Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, as a mawquf (halted) report, and he said: "Its isnad is sound." Al-Dhahabi criticised this, saying: "In it is Hanash al-Rahbi, and he is weak."]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So I seized them﴾, meaning I destroyed them for what they did of these sins and great transgressions. ﴿So how was My punishment?﴾, meaning how did My punishment of them and My retribution upon them reach you? It was severe, painful and agonising.

Qatadah said: "By Allah, it was severe."

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad, who is Ibn Abi Shaybah, narrated to us: Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Ya'qub ibn Utbah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas [[In T: "Imam Ahmad narrated with his chain from Ibn Abbas."]] [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from T and A.]], that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ affirmed a line of poetry by Umayyah, and he said:

"A man and a bull beneath his right foot,
the eagle for the other, and a lion lying in wait."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "True." Then he said:

"The sun rises every last night,
red, its color turning rosy..."

"It refuses, so it does not rise for us in its course
except punished, and except whipped."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "True" [[Al-Musnad (1/256). Al-Haythami said in Al-Majma' (8/127): "Its narrators are trustworthy, except that Ibn Ishaq is a mudallis (one who conceals his sources)."]].

This is a good chain, and it indicates that the bearers of the Throne are four today, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be eight, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And above them on that Day eight will bear the Throne of your Lord﴾ [al-Haqqah: 17].

Here there is a question: how is one to reconcile what is understood from this verse with the indication of this hadith, and with the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud:

Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr narrated to us, from Simak, from Abdullah ibn Umayrah [[In T: "Umrah."]], from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who said: I was in al-Batha in a group among whom was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a cloud passed over them. He looked at it and said: "What do you call this?" They said: "Clouds." He said: "And the rain-clouds?" They said: "And the rain-clouds." He said: "And the 'anan?" They said: "And the 'anan." (Abu Dawud said: I did not perfectly memorize the word 'anan.) He said: "Do you know the distance between the sky and the earth?" They said: "We do not know." He said: "The distance between them is either one, or two, or three [[In T and S: "or two or three."]] and seventy years. Then the sky above it is likewise," until he counted seven heavens. "Then above the seventh heaven is a sea, the distance between its bottom and its top like the distance from one heaven to another. Then above that are eight mountain goats, between their hooves and their knees is the distance from one heaven to another. Then upon their backs is the Throne, the distance between its bottom and its top like the distance from one heaven to another. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is above that." Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah then narrated it through Simak ibn Harb, with the same wording [[Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. (4723–4725); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3320); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (193).]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib."

This indicates that the bearers of the Throne are eight, as Shahr ibn Hawshab said: The bearers of the Throne are eight: four say, "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; to You is praise for Your forbearance after Your knowledge," and four say, "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; to You is praise for Your pardon after Your power."

For this reason, when they ask forgiveness for those who believe, they say: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾, meaning Your mercy encompasses their sins and their faults, and Your knowledge encompasses all their deeds [and their words] [[Addition from A.]], their movements and their stillnesses. ﴿So forgive those who repent and follow Your way﴾, meaning pardon the sinners when they repent, turn back, and abandon what they were engaged in, and follow what You have commanded them, of doing good and abandoning evil. ﴿And protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾, meaning keep them away from the punishment of the Blaze, which is the painful, agonizing torment.

﴿Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants﴾, meaning unite them with them, so that their eyes may be comforted by gathering in neighboring dwellings, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith, We will join their descendants with them and not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾ [al-Tur: 21], meaning We equalize all of them in rank so that their eyes are comforted. We did not diminish the higher to make him equal to the lower; rather, We raised the one lacking in deeds and equalized him with the one of abundant deeds, out of Our grace and bounty.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When a believer enters Paradise, he asks about his father, his son and his brother: "Where are they?" It is said: "They have not reached your rank in deeds." He says: "I only did deeds for myself and for them." So they are joined to him in rank. Then Sa'id ibn Jubayr recited this verse: ﴿Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾.

Mutarrif ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir said: The most sincere of Allah's servants toward the believers are the angels; then he recited this verse: ﴿Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You promised them﴾. And the most deceitful of Allah's servants toward the believers are the devils.

Here there is a question: how is one to reconcile what is understood from this verse with the indication of this hadith, and with the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud:

Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr narrated to us, from Simak, from Abdullah ibn Umayrah [[In T: "Umrah."]], from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who said: I was in al-Batha in a group among whom was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a cloud passed over them. He looked at it and said: "What do you call this?" They said: "Clouds." He said: "And the rain-clouds?" They said: "And the rain-clouds." He said: "And the 'anan?" They said: "And the 'anan." (Abu Dawud said: I did not perfectly memorize the word 'anan.) He said: "Do you know the distance between the sky and the earth?" They said: "We do not know." He said: "The distance between them is either one, or two, or three [[In T and S: "or two or three."]] and seventy years. Then the sky above it is likewise," until he counted seven heavens. "Then above the seventh heaven is a sea, the distance between its bottom and its top like the distance from one heaven to another. Then above that are eight mountain goats, between their hooves and their knees is the distance from one heaven to another. Then upon their backs is the Throne, the distance between its bottom and its top like the distance from one heaven to another. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is above that." Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah then narrated it through Simak ibn Harb, with the same wording [[Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. (4723–4725); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3320); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (193).]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib."

This indicates that the bearers of the Throne are eight, as Shahr ibn Hawshab said: The bearers of the Throne are eight: four say, "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; to You is praise for Your forbearance after Your knowledge," and four say, "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; to You is praise for Your pardon after Your power."

For this reason, when they ask forgiveness for those who believe, they say: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾, meaning Your mercy encompasses their sins and their faults, and Your knowledge encompasses all their deeds [and their words] [[Addition from A.]], their movements and their stillnesses. ﴿So forgive those who repent and follow Your way﴾, meaning pardon the sinners when they repent, turn back, and abandon what they were engaged in, and follow what You have commanded them, of doing good and abandoning evil. ﴿And protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾, meaning keep them away from the punishment of the Blaze, which is the painful, agonizing torment.

﴿Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants﴾, meaning unite them with them, so that their eyes may be comforted by gathering in neighboring dwellings, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith, We will join their descendants with them and not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾ [al-Tur: 21], meaning We equalize all of them in rank so that their eyes are comforted. We did not diminish the higher to make him equal to the lower; rather, We raised the one lacking in deeds and equalized him with the one of abundant deeds, out of Our grace and bounty.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When a believer enters Paradise, he asks about his father, his son and his brother: "Where are they?" It is said: "They have not reached your rank in deeds." He says: "I only did deeds for myself and for them." So they are joined to him in rank. Then Sa'id ibn Jubayr recited this verse: ﴿Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾.

Mutarrif ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir said: The most sincere of Allah's servants toward the believers are the angels; then he recited this verse: ﴿Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You promised them﴾. And the most deceitful of Allah's servants toward the believers are the devils.

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ means: the One who cannot be prevented or overpowered, and whatever He wills comes to be and whatever He does not will does not come to be; the Wise in Your statements and Your actions, in Your legislation and Your decree [[In A: "and Your power."]].

﴿And protect them from evil deeds﴾, meaning from committing them or from their consequences, for those upon whom they fall. ﴿And whoever You protect from evil deeds that Day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿You have indeed granted him mercy﴾, meaning You have shown him kindness and saved him from punishment. ﴿And that is the great triumph﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 40, verses 10–14:

The Exalted says, reporting about the disbelievers: they will be called out on the Day of Resurrection while they are in the depths of the Fire, writhing in it. This will be when they have experienced the punishment of Allah, which no one can withstand. At that point they will loathe themselves intensely and hate their own souls, because of the evil deeds they had sent ahead, which were the cause of their entry into the Fire. Then the angels will address them at that point with a loud address, calling out to them that Allah's loathing of them in the world, when faith was presented to them and they disbelieved, is greater than your loathing of yourselves today, O you who are being punished in this state.

Qatada said, regarding His words: ﴿Surely the loathing of Allah is greater than your loathing of yourselves, when you were called to faith but you disbelieved﴾, that it means: the loathing of Allah toward the people of misguidance, when faith was presented to them in the world and they abandoned it and refused to accept it, is greater than the loathing they feel for themselves when they witness the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Hasan al-Basri, Mujahid, al-Suddi, Dharr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hamdani, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said the same, may Allah have mercy on them.

As for His words: ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice"﴾, al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: this verse is like His saying: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die, then give you life again, then to Him you will be returned?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28]. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, Qatada and Abu Malik also said this, and this is the correct view about which there is no doubt or dispute.

Al-Suddi said: they were made to die in the world, then they were given life in their graves and were addressed; then they were made to die again, then they will be given life on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Zayd said: they were given life when the covenant was taken from them from the loins of Adam; then He created them in the wombs, then He caused them to die, then He will give them life on the Day of Resurrection.

These two opinions, those of al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd, are weak, because according to what they say it would require three lifes-givings and three deaths. The sound view is the saying of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas and those who followed them. The meaning of all of this is: the disbelievers will ask for a return (to the world) while they stand before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the plains of the Resurrection, as He said: ﴿If only you could see when the criminals will bow their heads before their Lord, saying, "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may work righteousness; indeed we are certain"﴾ [al-Sajdah: 12]. But they will not be answered. Then, when they see the Fire, witness it, stand over it, and look at the punishment and torment within it, they will ask for a return even more intensely than they asked the first time, but they will not be answered. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire and they say, "Oh, if only we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers." But rather, what they had concealed before has become apparent to them. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-An'am: 27–28]. When they enter the Fire and taste its heat, its roaring, its iron hooks and its shackles, their request for a return will be even more intense and greater: ﴿And they will cry out therein, "Our Lord, bring us out; we will work righteousness, other than what we used to do." Did We not give you a life long enough that whoever would remember could remember therein, and the warner came to you? So taste (the punishment), for there are no helpers for the wrongdoers﴾ [Fatir: 37]. ﴿"Our Lord, bring us out of it; then if we return (to disbelief), we will indeed be wrongdoers." He will say, "Remain in it and do not speak to Me."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 107–108]. In this noble verse they were gentle in their request and preceded their speech with an introduction, which is their saying: ﴿Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice﴾, meaning: Your power is great, for You gave us life after we had been dead, then You caused us to die, then You gave us life again, so You are capable of whatever You will. We have acknowledged our sins, and indeed we were wrongdoers against ourselves in the worldly abode. ﴿So is there any way to get out?﴾, meaning: will You respond to us by returning us to the worldly abode? You are capable of that, so that we may act differently from what we used to do. If we return to what we were in, then indeed we are wrongdoers. They were answered: there is no way for you to return to the worldly abode. Then He gave the reason for refusing that: your natures do not accept the truth and do not require it; rather, you deny it and reject it. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed.﴾, meaning: this is how you are, and even if you were returned to the world, you would be the same, as He said: ﴿And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-An'am: 28].

* *

As for His words: ﴿So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great﴾, meaning: He is the Judge over His creation, the Just who does not oppress. He guides whom He wills, leads astray whom He wills, has mercy on whom He wills, and punishes whom He wills. There is no god but Him.

* *

As for His words: ﴿It is He who shows you His signs﴾, meaning: He manifests His power to His creation through what they witness in His upper and lower creation of great signs that indicate the perfection of their Creator, Originator and Producer. ﴿And sends down for you provision from the sky﴾, which is the rain by which He brings forth from crops and fruits what is observed by the senses, with their differing colors, tastes, scents, shapes and hues, though it is one water. By His great power He distinguishes among these things. ﴿But none will be reminded﴾, meaning: none will take heed and reflect upon these things and draw evidence from them for the greatness of their Creator, ﴿except one who turns back (in repentance)﴾, meaning: one who is perceptive and turns back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So invoke Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, even if the disbelievers dislike it﴾, meaning: devote worship and supplication to Allah alone, and oppose the polytheists in their path and their creed.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hisham, meaning Ibn 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Tadrus al-Makki, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr used to say at the end of every prayer when he gave the salam: "There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise, and He is capable of everything. There is no power and no might except through Allah. There is no god but Allah, and we worship none but Him. To Him belongs the blessing and to Him belongs the favor, and to Him belongs the good praise. There is no god but Allah, sincere to Him in religion, even if the disbelievers dislike it." He said: and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to make tahlil with these words after every prayer. (al-Musnad, 4/4)

It was also narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, through several chains, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, Hajjaj ibn Abi 'Uthman, and Musa ibn 'Uqbah, all three from Abu al-Zubayr, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say after the prayer: "There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. [...]" and he mentioned its full text. (Sahih Muslim, no. 594)

It is also established in the Sahih, from Ibn al-Zubayr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say after the obligatory prayers: "There is no god but Allah, alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs the praise, and He is capable of everything. There is no power and no might except through Allah. There is no god but Allah, and we worship none but Him. To Him belongs the blessing and to Him belongs the favor, and to Him belongs the good praise. There is no god but Allah, sincere to Him in religion, even if the disbelievers dislike it." (Sahih Muslim, no. 594; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1506; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 1262)

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Rabi' narrated to us, al-Khasib ibn Nasih narrated to us, Salih, meaning al-Mizzi, narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Call upon Allah while you are certain of being answered, and know that Allah does not answer the supplication of a heart that is heedless and distracted."

[Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan, no. 3479, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih; al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (1/493) from 'Affan ibn Muslim and Musa ibn Isma'il; al-Tabarani narrated it in Kitab al-Du'a, no. 62, from Mukhallad ibn Khadash; all of them through the chain of Salih al-Mizzi. Al-Tabarani said in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: "No one narrated this hadith from Hisham ibn Hassan except Salih al-Mizzi." Its reliability depends on Salih al-Mizzi, who is abandoned (matruk) in hadith.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 40, verses 10–14:

The Exalted says, reporting about the disbelievers: they will be called out on the Day of Resurrection while they are in the depths of the Fire, writhing in it. This will be when they have experienced the punishment of Allah, which no one can withstand. At that point they will loathe themselves intensely and hate their own souls, because of the evil deeds they had sent ahead, which were the cause of their entry into the Fire. Qatada said, regarding His words: ﴿Surely the loathing of Allah is greater than your loathing of yourselves, when you were called to faith but you disbelieved﴾, that it means: the loathing of Allah toward the people of misguidance, when faith was presented to them in the world and they abandoned it and refused to accept it, is greater than the loathing they feel for themselves when they witness the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Hasan al-Basri, Mujahid, al-Suddi, Dharr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hamdani, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said the same, may Allah have mercy on them.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, Qatada and Abu Malik also said this, and this is the correct view about which there is no doubt or dispute.

The sound view is the saying of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas and those who followed them. It will come (later) in explanation that this is the distance between the Throne and the seventh earth, according to a group of the Salaf and the Khalaf, and it is the most likely view, if Allah the Exalted wills. Many have mentioned that the Throne is of red ruby, the breadth between its two sides being a journey of fifty thousand years, and its height above the seventh earth being a journey of fifty thousand years. And what has preceded in the hadith of "al-Awʿal" (the mountain goats) indicates its elevation above the seven heavens by a great distance.

The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, upon your heart, that you may be of the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 192–194]. Therefore He said: ﴿to warn of the Day of Meeting﴾. ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: "﴿The Day of Meeting﴾ is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, by which He warned His servants."

Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn ʿAbbas said: "On it, Adam and his last offspring will meet."

Ibn Zayd said: "On it, the servants will meet."

Qatadah, as-Suddi, Bilal ibn Sa'd, and Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "On it, the people of the heaven and the people of the earth will meet."

Qatadah also said: "On it, the people of the heaven and the people of the earth will meet, and the Creator and the creation."

Maymun ibn Mihran said: "On it, the oppressor and the oppressed will meet."

It may be said that the Day of Resurrection (the Day of Meeting) encompasses all of this, and includes that every doer will meet what he did of good and evil, as others have said.

* *

His saying: ﴿the Day they will come forth﴾ means: they will be apparent and exposed, all of them, with nothing to shelter them, shade them, or conceal them. Therefore He said: ﴿the Day they will come forth; nothing of them is hidden from Allah﴾, meaning: all of them are equal in His knowledge.

* *

Where are the kings of the earth? Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?"

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 40, verse 18–20:

"Yawm al-Azifah" (the Imminent Day) is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. It is so called because of its nearness, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The Imminent has drawn near. None besides Allah can reveal it﴾ [al-Najm 53:57–58]. He also says ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split﴾ [al-Qamar 54:1], ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near for them﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:1], and ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [al-Nahl 16:1], and ﴿But when they see it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieved will be distressed, and it will be said: "This is what you used to call for."﴾ [al-Mulk 67:27].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿when hearts reach the throats, choking [kazimin]﴾ [i.e., silent] [[addition from T.]], Qatadah said: The hearts will stand at the throats out of fear, neither coming out nor returning to their places. Ikrimah, al-Suddi and others said the same.

The meaning of ﴿kazimin﴾ is: silent, no one speaking except by His permission: ﴿The Day when the Spirit and the angels will stand in ranks; none will speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is correct﴾ [al-Naba' 78:38].

Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿kazimin﴾ means weeping.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend nor any intercessor who is obeyed﴾, it means: those who wronged themselves by associating others with Allah will have no close relative near them who could benefit them, nor any intercessor whose intercession would be accepted for them. Rather, all means of every good will have been cut off from them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾, Allah the Exalted informs of His complete knowledge encompassing all things, the great and the small, the minor and the major, the subtle and the fine, so that people will beware of His knowledge of them, be truly shy before Allah, fear Him with true fear, and watch over themselves as one who knows that He sees him. Indeed, He the Exalted knows the treacherous glance even if it displays trustworthiness, and He knows what lies hidden in the depths of the breasts of inner thoughts and secrets.

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾: it refers to a man who enters a household's house where there is a beautiful woman, or a beautiful woman passes by him and them. When they are heedless, he glances at her; when they notice, he lowers his gaze; when they are heedless again, he glances; when they notice, he lowers [his gaze from her]. Allah has known from his heart that he wishes he could see her private part. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Al-Dahhak said: "the treachery of the eyes" is winking, and a man's saying "I saw" when he did not see, or "I did not see" when he did see.

Ibn 'Abbas also said: Allah the Exalted knows, from the eye in its looking, whether it intends betrayal or not. Mujahid and Qatadah said the same.

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying ﴿and what the breasts conceal﴾: He knows, if you have power over her, whether you will commit adultery with her or not.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿and what the breasts conceal﴾ means: [of] the whisperings.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah the Exalted says: "Have these deniers of your message, O Muhammad, not travelled in the land, so that they might see what was the end of those who came before them?" That is, of the nations that denied the prophets, what punishment and retribution befell them, even though they were stronger than these people in power, ﴿and in traces left upon the earth﴾. That is, they left marks upon the earth through buildings, monuments and dwellings that these people are not able to match, as He said: ﴿And We had established them in that wherein We have not established you﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 26], and He said: ﴿And they tilled the earth and populated it more than these have populated it﴾ [al-Rum: 9]. That is: despite this great strength and severe might, Allah seized them for their sins, which were their disbelief in their messengers. ﴿And they had none to protect them from Allah﴾. That is: no one repelled the punishment of Allah from them, none turned it back from them, and no protector shielded them.

Then He mentioned the reason for His seizing them and the sins they committed and perpetrated, saying: ﴿That was because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs﴾. That is, with evident signs and decisive arguments. ﴿So they disbelieved﴾. That is, despite this clarification and proof, they disbelieved and denied. ﴿So Allah seized them﴾. That is, He destroyed them and annihilated them, and the disbelievers will have similar fates. ﴿Indeed, He is Strong and severe in punishment﴾. That is, He possesses great power and severe seizing. And He is ﴿severe in punishment﴾, meaning His punishment is painful, harsh and grievous. May Allah protect us from it.

That is, He destroyed them and annihilated them, and the disbelievers will have similar fates. ﴿Indeed, He is Strong and severe in punishment﴾. That is, He possesses great power and severe seizing. And He is ﴿severe in punishment﴾, meaning His punishment is painful, harsh and grievous. May Allah protect us from it.

Allah the Exalted says, consoling His Prophet (ﷺ) for the denial of those among his people who denied him, and giving him good news that the final outcome and victory belong to him in this world and the Hereafter, just as it happened to Musa ibn Imran (Moses) [[In manuscript S: "to His Prophet Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him."]]. Allah sent him with clear signs and manifest proofs [[In manuscript T: "and the clear evidences."]]. Therefore He said: ﴿With Our signs and a clear authority﴾. The authority (sultan) is the argument and the proof.

﴿To Pharaoh﴾, the king of the Copts in the land of Egypt, ﴿and Haman﴾, who was his minister in his kingdom, ﴿and Qarun﴾, who was among the richest people of his time in wealth and trade. ﴿They said: "A sorcerer, a liar."﴾ That is, they denied him and made him out to be a sorcerer, a deceiver, a fabricator and a liar concerning Allah's sending him. This is like His saying: ﴿Likewise, no messenger came to those before them except that they said, "A sorcerer or a madman." Did they bequeath this saying to one another? Rather, they are a transgressing people.﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 51:52–53].

Qatadah said: "This was one command after another."

[Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/414).]

The well-known view is that this believing man was a Copt from the family of Pharaoh.

As-Suddi said: he was a cousin of Pharaoh. It is also said that he was the one who was saved along with Musa. Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] preferred this view.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (24/38).]] He rejected the view of those who held that the man was an Israelite, because Pharaoh was moved by his words and listened to him, and restrained himself from killing Musa, peace be upon him. Had he been an Israelite, he would have been swiftly punished, since he belonged to them.[[In T: "yuqabil" (confronted). In S and T: "muttahaman" (accused).]]

Ibn Juraij related from Ibn 'Abbas: "None from the family of Pharaoh believed except this man and the wife of Pharaoh, and the one who said: ﴿O Musa, the chiefs are conspiring against you to kill you﴾ [al-Qasas 28:20]." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

This man had been concealing his faith from his Coptic people. He did not reveal it until this day, when Pharaoh said: ﴿Let me kill Musa﴾. Then a zeal for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, seized the man, and "The best jihad is a word of justice before an oppressive ruler," as this hadith has established. There is no greater word before Pharaoh than his statement: ﴿Will you kill a man merely for saying, "My Lord is Allah"?﴾ [i.e., because he says, "My Lord is Allah"].[[Addition from T, S, A.]] Except what al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih, where he said:

"'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi narrated to me, and 'Urwah ibn al-Zubair narrated to me, saying: I said to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As: Tell me of the worst thing the polytheists did to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was praying in the courtyard of the Ka'bah, 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt came, seized the shoulder of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), twisted his garment around his neck, and choked him severely. Then Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, came, seized his shoulder, pushed him away from the Prophet (ﷺ), and said: ﴿Will you kill a man merely for saying, "My Lord is Allah," when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord?﴾"

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it from the hadith of al-Awza'i. He said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq followed him, from Yahya ibn 'Urwah, from his father, with the same wording.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4815.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, 'Abdah narrated to us from Hisham, meaning Ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Amr ibn al-'As, that he was asked: What is the worst you saw Quraysh inflict upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? He said: One day he passed by them, and they said to him: "Do you forbid us from worshipping what our fathers worshipped?" He said: "I am that one." They rose against him and seized the hems of his garments. I saw Abu Bakr embracing him from behind, crying out at the top of his voice, and his eyes were flowing with tears, and he was saying: "O people, ﴿Will you kill a man merely for saying, "My Lord is Allah," when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord?﴾" until he finished the whole verse.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it in the same way from the hadith of 'Abdah, making it a narration of 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him.[[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11462.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿and he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord﴾ means: How can you kill a man for saying "My Lord is Allah," when he has presented to you the proof of the truth of what he has brought you? Then he came down to their level in the discussion and said: ﴿If he is a liar, his lie will be upon him; but if he is truthful, some of what he threatens you with will befall you﴾. That is: if he has not shown you the truth of what he brought, then wisdom, sound judgment and prudence require that you leave him and his self alone, and do not harm him. If he is a liar, Allah will requite him for his lie with punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And if he is truthful and you have harmed him, some of what he threatens you with will befall you, for he warns you that if you oppose him he will bring punishment upon you in this world and the Hereafter. Thus it is possible in your view that he is truthful, and therefore you should not confront him, but leave him and his people to call them and to follow him.

In the same way, Allah informed us about Musa, peace be upon him, that he asked Pharaoh and his people for a truce, in His saying: ﴿And We had already tested the people of Pharaoh before them, when there came to them a noble messenger: "Deliver to me the servants of Allah; I am a trustworthy messenger to you. And do not exalt yourselves against Allah; I am bringing you a manifest authority. And I have sought refuge with my Lord and your Lord lest you stone me. And if you do not believe me, then leave me alone"﴾ [al-Dukhan 44:17–21]. In the same way the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Quraysh that they should leave him to call the servants of Allah to Allah, [Exalted is He],[[Addition from A.]] and not touch him with harm, and that they should maintain the kinship between him and them by refraining from harming him. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it except love for my near kin﴾ [al-Shura 42:23]. That is: except that you not harm me regarding the kinship between me and you; so do not harm me, and leave me between myself and the people. On this basis the truce was concluded at al-Hudaybiyyah, and it was a manifest victory.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor, a liar﴾ means: If this man, who claims that Allah sent him to you, were a liar as you claim, his affair would not be consistent; it would be in utmost contradiction and disorder in his sayings and actions for everyone to see. But we see his affair to be sound and his method upright. Had he been one of the transgressing liars, Allah would not have guided him and directed him to the orderly affair and conduct that you see in him.

Then the believer said, warning his people of the removal of Allah's blessing from them and the descent of Allah's vengeance upon them: ﴿O my people, the kingdom is yours today, prevailing in the land﴾. That is: Allah has bestowed upon you this dominion and prominence in the land, with an effective word and wide influence. So safeguard this blessing by thanking Allah and by affirming His Messenger (ﷺ), and beware of Allah's vengeance if you deny His Messenger. ﴿Then who will help us against the might of Allah if it comes upon us?﴾ That is: these armies and these soldiers will not avail you, nor will they ward off from us any part of Allah's might should He intend us harm.

﴿Pharaoh said﴾ to his people, rejecting what this righteous, dutiful, rightly guided man advised, the man who was more worthy of the kingdom than Pharaoh: ﴿I show you only what I see﴾. That is: I say to you and advise you only what I see for myself. Pharaoh lied, for he was certain of the truthfulness of Musa in what he brought of the message: ﴿He said: "You certainly know that none has sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence"﴾ [al-Isra 17:102]. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance﴾ [al-Naml 27:14].

So his saying ﴿I show you only what I see﴾ was a lie and a fabrication, and a betrayal of Allah, His Messenger, and his subjects; he deceived them and did not advise them. Likewise his saying: ﴿And I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾. That is: I call you only to the path of truth, sincerity and right guidance. He lied in this too, even though his people obeyed and followed him. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿So they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not right﴾ [Hud 11:97], and He, Exalted, said: ﴿And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:79]. And in the hadith: "There is no ruler who dies on the day he dies while deceiving his subjects, except that he will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, though its fragrance can be detected from a distance of five hundred years."[[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, nos. 7150 and 7151, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 142, in a similar wording, from the hadith of Ma'qil ibn Yasar, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

The well-known view is that this believing man was a Copt from the family of Pharaoh.

As-Suddi said: he was a cousin of Pharaoh. It is also said that he was the one who was saved along with Musa. Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] preferred this view.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (24/38).]] He rejected the view of those who held that the man was an Israelite, because Pharaoh was moved by his words and listened to him, and restrained himself from killing Musa, peace be upon him. Had he been an Israelite, he would have been swiftly punished, since he belonged to them.[[In T: "yuqabil" (confronted). In S and T: "muttahaman" (accused).]]

Ibn Juraij related from Ibn 'Abbas: "None from the family of Pharaoh believed except this man and the wife of Pharaoh, and the one who said: ﴿O Musa, the chiefs are conspiring against you to kill you﴾ [al-Qasas 28:20]." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

This man had been concealing his faith from his Coptic people. He did not reveal it until this day, when Pharaoh said: ﴿Let me kill Musa﴾. Then a zeal for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, seized the man, and "The best jihad is a word of justice before an oppressive ruler," as this hadith has established. There is no greater word before Pharaoh than his statement: ﴿Will you kill a man merely for saying, "My Lord is Allah"?﴾ [i.e., because he says, "My Lord is Allah"].[[Addition from T, S, A.]] Except what al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih, where he said:

"'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi narrated to me, and 'Urwah ibn al-Zubair narrated to me, saying: I said to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As: Tell me of the worst thing the polytheists did to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was praying in the courtyard of the Ka'bah, 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt came, seized the shoulder of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), twisted his garment around his neck, and choked him severely. Then Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, came, seized his shoulder, pushed him away from the Prophet (ﷺ), and said: ﴿Will you kill a man merely for saying, "My Lord is Allah," when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord?﴾"

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it from the hadith of al-Awza'i. He said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq followed him, from Yahya ibn 'Urwah, from his father, with the same wording.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4815.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, 'Abdah narrated to us from Hisham, meaning Ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Amr ibn al-'As, that he was asked: What is the worst you saw Quraysh inflict upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? He said: One day he passed by them, and they said to him: "Do you forbid us from worshipping what our fathers worshipped?" He said: "I am that one." They rose against him and seized the hems of his garments. I saw Abu Bakr embracing him from behind, crying out at the top of his voice, and his eyes were flowing with tears, and he was saying: "O people, ﴿Will you kill a man merely for saying, "My Lord is Allah," when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord?﴾" until he finished the whole verse.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it in the same way from the hadith of 'Abdah, making it a narration of 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him.[[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11462.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿and he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord﴾ means: How can you kill a man for saying "My Lord is Allah," when he has presented to you the proof of the truth of what he has brought you? Then he came down to their level in the discussion and said: ﴿If he is a liar, his lie will be upon him; but if he is truthful, some of what he threatens you with will befall you﴾. That is: if he has not shown you the truth of what he brought, then wisdom, sound judgment and prudence require that you leave him and his self alone, and do not harm him. If he is a liar, Allah will requite him for his lie with punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And if he is truthful and you have harmed him, some of what he threatens you with will befall you, for he warns you that if you oppose him he will bring punishment upon you in this world and the Hereafter. Thus it is possible in your view that he is truthful, and therefore you should not confront him, but leave him and his people to call them and to follow him.

In the same way, Allah informed us about Musa, peace be upon him, that he asked Pharaoh and his people for a truce, in His saying: ﴿And We had already tested the people of Pharaoh before them, when there came to them a noble messenger: "Deliver to me the servants of Allah; I am a trustworthy messenger to you. And do not exalt yourselves against Allah; I am bringing you a manifest authority. And I have sought refuge with my Lord and your Lord lest you stone me. And if you do not believe me, then leave me alone"﴾ [al-Dukhan 44:17–21]. In the same way the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Quraysh that they should leave him to call the servants of Allah to Allah, [Exalted is He],[[Addition from A.]] and not touch him with harm, and that they should maintain the kinship between him and them by refraining from harming him. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it except love for my near kin﴾ [al-Shura 42:23]. That is: except that you not harm me regarding the kinship between me and you; so do not harm me, and leave me between myself and the people. On this basis the truce was concluded at al-Hudaybiyyah, and it was a manifest victory.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor, a liar﴾ means: If this man, who claims that Allah sent him to you, were a liar as you claim, his affair would not be consistent; it would be in utmost contradiction and disorder in his sayings and actions for everyone to see. But we see his affair to be sound and his method upright. Had he been one of the transgressing liars, Allah would not have guided him and directed him to the orderly affair and conduct that you see in him.

Then the believer said, warning his people of the removal of Allah's blessing from them and the descent of Allah's vengeance upon them: ﴿O my people, the kingdom is yours today, prevailing in the land﴾. That is: Allah has bestowed upon you this dominion and prominence in the land, with an effective word and wide influence. So safeguard this blessing by thanking Allah and by affirming His Messenger (ﷺ), and beware of Allah's vengeance if you deny His Messenger. ﴿Then who will help us against the might of Allah if it comes upon us?﴾ That is: these armies and these soldiers will not avail you, nor will they ward off from us any part of Allah's might should He intend us harm.

﴿Pharaoh said﴾ to his people, rejecting what this righteous, dutiful, rightly guided man advised, the man who was more worthy of the kingdom than Pharaoh: ﴿I show you only what I see﴾. That is: I say to you and advise you only what I see for myself. Pharaoh lied, for he was certain of the truthfulness of Musa in what he brought of the message: ﴿He said: "You certainly know that none has sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence"﴾ [al-Isra 17:102]. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance﴾ [al-Naml 27:14].

So his saying ﴿I show you only what I see﴾ was a lie and a fabrication, and a betrayal of Allah, His Messenger, and his subjects; he deceived them and did not advise them. Likewise his saying: ﴿And I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾. That is: I call you only to the path of truth, sincerity and right guidance. He lied in this too, even though his people obeyed and followed him. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿So they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not right﴾ [Hud 11:97], and He, Exalted, said: ﴿And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:79]. And in the hadith: "There is no ruler who dies on the day he dies while deceiving his subjects, except that he will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, though its fragrance can be detected from a distance of five hundred years."[[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, nos. 7150 and 7151, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 142, in a similar wording, from the hadith of Ma'qil ibn Yasar, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

This is a report from God, exalted and majestic, about this righteous man, the believer from the family of Pharaoh. He warned his people of God's punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and said: ﴿O my people, indeed I fear for you a day like the day of the factions﴾, meaning those who denied the messengers of God in ancient times, such as the people of Noah, ʿAd, and Thamud, and the disbelieving nations after them. [He meant] how God's punishment befell them, and no one could repel it from them, and no one could turn it away from them.

﴿And God does not want injustice for the servants﴾, meaning God only destroyed them because of their sins, their denial of His messengers, and their opposition to His command. He carried out His decree upon them. Then he said: ﴿And O my people, indeed I fear for you the day of calling out﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection. It was named that for the following reasons. Some of them said: as occurs in the hadith of the Trumpet, when the earth is shaken and split from one end to the other, and it heaves and quakes, people see this and flee in fear, calling out to one another.

Others, including al-Dahhak, said: rather, it is when Hell is brought forward, and people flee from it in fright, and the angels meet them and turn them back to the place of assembly. This is the meaning of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And the angel will be upon its sides﴾ [al-Haqqah 69:17], and His statement ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass through the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through; you will not pass except with authority﴾ [al-Rahman 55:33].

It has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, and al-Dahhak that they recited it as "yawm al-tanaddd" with the letter dal doubled, from nadda al-baʿir, meaning when the camel bolts and runs off.

It was also said: because the scale is in the charge of an angel, and when he weighs a servant's deeds, if they outweigh, he calls out in a loud voice: "Surely so-and-so son of so-and-so has been made happy with a happiness after which he will never be miserable forever." And if his deeds are light, he calls out: "Surely so-and-so son of so-and-so has become miserable."

Qatadah said: each group is called by their deeds. The people of Paradise are called "People of Paradise," and the people of the Fire are called "People of the Fire."

It was also said: it is named so because the people of Paradise call out to the people of the Fire: ﴿That we have found what our Lord promised us to be true; so have you found what your Lord promised to be true?" They say, "Yes"﴾ [al-Aʿraf 7:44]. And the people of the Fire call out to the people of Paradise: ﴿Pour upon us some water or some of what God has provided you." They say, "Indeed, God has forbidden them to the disbelievers"﴾ [al-Aʿraf 7:50]. And the calling of the companions of al-Aʿraf to the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, as mentioned in Surah al-Aʿraf.

Al-Baghawi and others chose that it was named so because of all of these together. This is a good and sound view, and God knows best. [Source: Maʿalim al-Tanzil by al-Baghawi (7/147, 148).]

* *

Therefore He said: ﴿You will have no protector from God﴾, meaning you will have no preventer who can keep you from God's punishment and torment. ﴿And whoever God leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾, meaning whomever God has led astray [God], there is no guide for him besides Him.

His statement: ﴿The day you turn back fleeing﴾, meaning running away in fright, ﴿No refuge! There is no refuge. To your Lord that day is the place of settlement﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:11–12]. Therefore He said: ﴿You will have no protector from God﴾, meaning you will have no preventer who can keep you from God's punishment and torment. ﴿And whoever God leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾, meaning whomever God has led astray [God], there is no guide for him besides Him.

* *

His statement: ﴿And Joseph had already come to you before with clear evidences﴾, meaning the people of Egypt. God had sent to them a messenger before Moses, and he was Joseph, peace be upon him. He was the ruler of the people of Egypt, and he was a messenger calling to God his nation, the Copts. But they did not obey him at that time except for the sake of the office and worldly status. Therefore He said: ﴿And you remained in doubt about what he brought you, until when he died, you said, "God will never send after him a messenger"﴾, meaning you despaired and said, out of greed [for worldly gain]: ﴿God will never send after him a messenger.﴾ This was due to their disbelief and denial. ﴿Thus does God leave astray whoever is a transgressor and doubter﴾, meaning, like your state now.

Then He said: ﴿Those who dispute concerning the verses of God without authority having come to them﴾, meaning those who repel the truth with falsehood, and argue against proofs without any evidence or proof from God with them. Therefore He said: ﴿Thus does God seal the heart of every arrogant tyrant﴾, meaning from following the truth, ﴿tyrant﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from ʿIkrimah, and it is related from al-Shaʿbi, that both of them said: a person is not called a tyrant (jabbar) until he kills two souls.

Abu ʿImran al-Jawni and Qatadah said: the sign of tyrants is killing without right.

This is a report from God, exalted and majestic, about this righteous man, the believer from the family of Pharaoh. [He meant] how God's punishment befell them, and no one could repel it from them, and no one could turn it away from them.

﴿And God does not want injustice for the servants﴾, meaning God only destroyed them because of their sins, their denial of His messengers, and their opposition to His command. And if his deeds are light, he calls out: "Surely so-and-so son of so-and-so has become miserable."

Qatadah said: each group is called by their deeds. The people of Paradise are called "People of Paradise," and the people of the Fire are called "People of the Fire."

It was also said: it is named so because the people of Paradise call out to the people of the Fire: ﴿That we have found what our Lord promised us to be true; so have you found what your Lord promised to be true?" They say, "Yes"﴾ [al-Aʿraf 7:44]. And the people of the Fire call out to the people of Paradise: ﴿Pour upon us some water or some of what God has provided you." They say, "Indeed, God has forbidden them to the disbelievers"﴾ [al-Aʿraf 7:50]. The believing man said to his people, from among those who were rebellious, transgressed, preferred the worldly life, and forgot the Almighty, the Most High, so he said to them: ﴿O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the path of right conduct﴾

Not as Pharaoh lied in his statement: ﴿And I show you only the path of right conduct﴾.

Then he made them renounce the worldly life, which they had [indeed] preferred over the Hereafter, and which had diverted them from believing in the Messenger of Allah, Musa (ﷺ). So he said: ﴿O my people, this worldly life is only a passing enjoyment﴾, meaning: it is few, perishable, transient, and soon it will go away and vanish. ﴿And indeed the Hereafter is the abode of settlement﴾, meaning: the abode that has no cessation, no transfer from it, and no departure from it to anything else; rather, it is either bliss or hellfire. For this reason He said: ﴿Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like﴾, meaning: one like it. ﴿And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise, being provided therein without account﴾, meaning: it is not measured by a reward; rather, Allah rewards him with abundant reward that has no end and no exhaustion.

The believer said to them: "What is wrong with me that I call you to salvation, which is worshipping God alone, with no partner, and affirming His Messenger whom He sent, while you call me to the Fire? You call me to disbelieve in God and to associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge"; that is, ignorance without any proof. "And I call you to the Mighty, the Most Forgiving": that is, He, in His might and majesty, forgives the sin of whoever turns to Him in repentance. "There is no doubt that what you call me to has no call in this world or in the Hereafter": "la jaram" (without doubt) means "truly."

Al-Suddi and Ibn Jarir said: the meaning of His words "la jaram" is "truly."

Al-Dahhak said: "la jaram" means "there is no lie."

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: "la jaram" means "yes indeed; what you call me to, of idols and rivals, has no call in this world or in the Hereafter."

Mujahid said: the idol is nothing.

Qatadah said: it means the idol neither benefits nor harms.

Al-Suddi said: it does not answer its caller, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

This is like His saying: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than God those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their calling? And when mankind are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 5-6], and ﴿If you call them, they will not hear your call; and if they heard, they would not respond to you﴾ [Fatir: 14].

* *

His words "And that our return is to God": that is, in the Hereafter, where He will recompense each person according to his deeds. For this reason He said: "And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire": that is, they will abide therein because of their transgression, which is their associating others with God.

"So you will remember what I tell you": that is, you will soon know the truth of what I commanded you and forbade you, what I advised you and made clear to you, and you will remember it and regret, when regret will not benefit you. "And I entrust my affair to God": that is, I rely upon God and seek His help, and I cut off from you and distance myself from you. "Indeed God is Seeing of the servants": that is, He sees them, so He guides whoever deserves guidance, and leads astray whoever deserves to be led astray. To Him belongs the conclusive proof, the perfect wisdom, and the effective decree.

* *

His words [Exalted is He] (added from manuscript A): ﴿So God saved him from the evils of what they plotted﴾: that is, in this world and in the Hereafter. In this world, God saved him along with Musa, peace be upon him. In the Hereafter, He saved him by admitting him to Paradise. ﴿And there befell the people of Pharaoh the worst of punishment﴾, which is drowning in the sea, and then their transfer from it to the Hellfire. Their spirits are presented to the Fire morning and evening until the Hour arises. When the Day of Resurrection comes, their spirits and bodies will be gathered in the Fire. For this reason He said: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established: "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment"﴾: that is, the most painful and most severe in retribution. This verse is a major foundation for the proof used by the People of the Sunnah for the punishment of the barzakh (intermediate state) in the graves, which is His saying: ﴿The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾.

However, there is a question here. There is no doubt that this verse is Meccan, and they have used it as evidence for the punishment of the grave in the barzakh. Imam Ahmad has said:

Hashim, that is Ibn al-Qasim Abu al-Nadr, narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Sa'id, that is Ibn Amr ibn Sa'id ibn al-As, narrated to us: Sa'id, meaning his father, narrated to us from Aishah: that a Jewish woman used to serve her, and whenever Aishah did any good to her, the Jewish woman would say to her: "May God protect you from the punishment of the grave." She said: The Messenger of God ﷺ entered upon me, and I said: "O Messenger of God, is there a punishment of the grave before the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "No. Why do you ask?" She said: "This Jewish woman; whenever we do any good to her, she says: 'May God protect you from the punishment of the grave.'" He said: "The Jews have lied, and they are even greater liars against God. There is no punishment before the Day of Resurrection." Then he remained as long as God willed, and then one day he went out at midday, wrapped in his garment, his eyes reddened, calling out at the top of his voice: "The grave is like pieces of the dark night. O people, if you knew what I know, you would weep much and laugh little. O people, seek refuge with God from the punishment of the grave, for the punishment of the grave is true." [Al-Musnad (6/81)].

This is a sound chain of narration according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim, though they did not record it.

Ahmad also narrated: Yazid narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah: a Jewish woman asked her and she gave her something, and she said to her: "May God protect you from the punishment of the grave." Aishah denied this. When she saw the Messenger of God ﷺ she told him, and he said: "No." Aishah said: Then the Messenger of God ﷺ said to us afterward: "Indeed it has been revealed to me that you will be tested in your graves." This is also according to their conditions [Al-Musnad (6/238)].

So it is said: What is the reconciliation between this and the verse being Meccan, while it contains evidence for the punishment of the barzakh? The answer is that the verse indicates the presentation of the spirits to the Fire morning and evening in the barzakh, but there is no indication in it that their suffering is connected to their bodies in the graves. It may be specific to the spirit. As for the attainment of this by the body and its suffering because of it, only the Sunnah has indicated it, in the accepted hadiths to be mentioned below.

It may also be said that this verse only indicates the punishment of disbelievers in the barzakh, and it does not follow from this that a believer is punished in his grave for a sin. Among what indicates this is what Imam Ahmad narrated:

Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God ﷺ entered upon her while a Jewish woman was with her, saying: "Did you know that you will be tested in your graves?" The Messenger of God ﷺ was alarmed and said: "Only the Jews will be tested." Aishah said: We stayed for some nights, then the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Did you know that it has been revealed to me that you will be tested in the graves?" Aishah said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ afterward seeking refuge from the punishment of the grave.

Muslim also narrated it in this way, from Harun ibn Sa'id and Harmalah, both from Ibn Wahb, from Yunus ibn Yazid al-Aili, from al-Zuhri, with it [Al-Musnad (6/248) and Sahih Muslim no. (584)].

It may also be said: this verse indicates the punishment of the spirits in the barzakh, and it does not follow that it is connected to the bodies in their graves. So when it was revealed to him concerning this, specifically, he sought refuge from it. God, Glorified and Exalted, knows best.

Al-Bukhari also narrated from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha, from his father, from Masruq, from Aishah, may God be pleased with her, that a Jewish woman entered upon her and said: "May God protect you from the punishment of the grave." Aishah asked the Messenger of God ﷺ about the punishment of the grave, and he said: "Yes, the punishment of the grave is true." Aishah said: I never saw the Messenger of God ﷺ after that pray a prayer without seeking refuge from the punishment of the grave [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1372)].

This shows that he quickly affirmed the Jewish woman's report and confirmed it. In the earlier reports, he denied it until revelation came to him. Perhaps these are two separate incidents, and God knows best. The hadiths on the punishment of the grave are very numerous.

Qatadah said concerning His words ﴿morning and evening﴾: "In the morning and evening, as long as the world remains. It will be said to them: 'O people of Pharaoh, these are your dwellings,' as rebuke, retribution, and humiliation for them."

Ibn Zayd said: "They are in it today; they are brought in the morning and evening until the Hour arises."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, al-Muharibi narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Tharwan, from Hudhayl, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: "The spirits of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds, roaming in Paradise wherever they wish. The spirits of the children of the believers are in the crops of sparrows, roaming in Paradise wherever they wish, then they take refuge in lamps hanging from the Throne. The spirits of the people of Pharaoh are in the crops of black birds, which go forth to Hell in the morning and return to it in the evening; that is their presentation."

This was also narrated by al-Thawri from Abu Qays from al-Hudhayl ibn Shurahbil, as his own statement about the spirits of the people of Pharaoh. Al-Suddi also said likewise.
