His words [Exalted is He] (added from manuscript A): ﴿So God saved him from the evils of what they plotted﴾: that is, in this world and in the Hereafter. In this world, God saved him along with Musa, peace be upon him. In the Hereafter, He saved him by admitting him to Paradise. ﴿And there befell the people of Pharaoh the worst of punishment﴾, which is drowning in the sea, and then their transfer from it to the Hellfire. Their spirits are presented to the Fire morning and evening until the Hour arises. When the Day of Resurrection comes, their spirits and bodies will be gathered in the Fire. For this reason He said: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established: "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment"﴾: that is, the most painful and most severe in retribution. This verse is a major foundation for the proof used by the People of the Sunnah for the punishment of the barzakh (intermediate state) in the graves, which is His saying: ﴿The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾.

However, there is a question here. There is no doubt that this verse is Meccan, and they have used it as evidence for the punishment of the grave in the barzakh. Imam Ahmad has said:

Hashim, that is Ibn al-Qasim Abu al-Nadr, narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Sa'id, that is Ibn Amr ibn Sa'id ibn al-As, narrated to us: Sa'id, meaning his father, narrated to us from Aishah: that a Jewish woman used to serve her, and whenever Aishah did any good to her, the Jewish woman would say to her: "May God protect you from the punishment of the grave." She said: The Messenger of God ﷺ entered upon me, and I said: "O Messenger of God, is there a punishment of the grave before the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "No. Why do you ask?" She said: "This Jewish woman; whenever we do any good to her, she says: 'May God protect you from the punishment of the grave.'" He said: "The Jews have lied, and they are even greater liars against God. There is no punishment before the Day of Resurrection." Then he remained as long as God willed, and then one day he went out at midday, wrapped in his garment, his eyes reddened, calling out at the top of his voice: "The grave is like pieces of the dark night. O people, if you knew what I know, you would weep much and laugh little. O people, seek refuge with God from the punishment of the grave, for the punishment of the grave is true." [Al-Musnad (6/81)].

This is a sound chain of narration according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim, though they did not record it.

Ahmad also narrated: Yazid narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah: a Jewish woman asked her and she gave her something, and she said to her: "May God protect you from the punishment of the grave." Aishah denied this. When she saw the Messenger of God ﷺ she told him, and he said: "No." Aishah said: Then the Messenger of God ﷺ said to us afterward: "Indeed it has been revealed to me that you will be tested in your graves." This is also according to their conditions [Al-Musnad (6/238)].

So it is said: What is the reconciliation between this and the verse being Meccan, while it contains evidence for the punishment of the barzakh? The answer is that the verse indicates the presentation of the spirits to the Fire morning and evening in the barzakh, but there is no indication in it that their suffering is connected to their bodies in the graves. It may be specific to the spirit. As for the attainment of this by the body and its suffering because of it, only the Sunnah has indicated it, in the accepted hadiths to be mentioned below.

It may also be said that this verse only indicates the punishment of disbelievers in the barzakh, and it does not follow from this that a believer is punished in his grave for a sin. Among what indicates this is what Imam Ahmad narrated:

Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God ﷺ entered upon her while a Jewish woman was with her, saying: "Did you know that you will be tested in your graves?" The Messenger of God ﷺ was alarmed and said: "Only the Jews will be tested." Aishah said: We stayed for some nights, then the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Did you know that it has been revealed to me that you will be tested in the graves?" Aishah said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ afterward seeking refuge from the punishment of the grave.

Muslim also narrated it in this way, from Harun ibn Sa'id and Harmalah, both from Ibn Wahb, from Yunus ibn Yazid al-Aili, from al-Zuhri, with it [Al-Musnad (6/248) and Sahih Muslim no. (584)].

It may also be said: this verse indicates the punishment of the spirits in the barzakh, and it does not follow that it is connected to the bodies in their graves. So when it was revealed to him concerning this, specifically, he sought refuge from it. God, Glorified and Exalted, knows best.

Al-Bukhari also narrated from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha, from his father, from Masruq, from Aishah, may God be pleased with her, that a Jewish woman entered upon her and said: "May God protect you from the punishment of the grave." Aishah asked the Messenger of God ﷺ about the punishment of the grave, and he said: "Yes, the punishment of the grave is true." Aishah said: I never saw the Messenger of God ﷺ after that pray a prayer without seeking refuge from the punishment of the grave [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1372)].

This shows that he quickly affirmed the Jewish woman's report and confirmed it. In the earlier reports, he denied it until revelation came to him. Perhaps these are two separate incidents, and God knows best. The hadiths on the punishment of the grave are very numerous.

Qatadah said concerning His words ﴿morning and evening﴾: "In the morning and evening, as long as the world remains. It will be said to them: 'O people of Pharaoh, these are your dwellings,' as rebuke, retribution, and humiliation for them."

Ibn Zayd said: "They are in it today; they are brought in the morning and evening until the Hour arises."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, al-Muharibi narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Tharwan, from Hudhayl, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: "The spirits of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds, roaming in Paradise wherever they wish. The spirits of the children of the believers are in the crops of sparrows, roaming in Paradise wherever they wish, then they take refuge in lamps hanging from the Throne. The spirits of the people of Pharaoh are in the crops of black birds, which go forth to Hell in the morning and return to it in the evening; that is their presentation."

This was also narrated by al-Thawri from Abu Qays from al-Hudhayl ibn Shurahbil, as his own statement about the spirits of the people of Pharaoh. Al-Suddi also said likewise.

In the hadith of the Night Journey, narrated from Abu Harun al-Abdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, he said in it: "Then I was taken to a great number of God's creatures, men, each of whom had a belly like a large house, bound along the road of the people of Pharaoh, and the people of Pharaoh were presented to the Fire morning and evening. ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established: 'Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment'﴾. The people of Pharaoh were like camels marked for distinction, trampling on stones and trees, and not understanding."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Zayd ibn Akhram narrated to us, Amir ibn Mudrik al-Harithi narrated to us, Utbah, meaning Ibn Yaqzan, narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "No one from among the Muslims or disbelievers does a good deed except that God rewards him." He said: We said: "O Messenger of God, what is the reward of the disbeliever?" He said: "If he has joined ties of kinship, or given charity, or done a good deed, God will reward him with wealth, children, health, and the like." We said: "What is his reward in the Hereafter?" He said: "A punishment less than the punishment," and he recited: ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment﴾. Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad from Zayd ibn Akhram, then said: "We do not know a chain for it other than this" [Musnad al-Bazzar no. (945), Kashf al-Astar; al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/253) through Ali ibn al-Husayn, and said: "Its chain is sound, but they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi criticized him. I say: in it is Utbah ibn Yaqzan, who is weak].

Ibn Jarir said: Abd al-Karim ibn Abi Umayr narrated to us, Hammad ibn Muhammad al-Fazari al-Balkhi narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Awza'i, and a man asked him, saying: "May God have mercy on you. We have seen birds emerging from the sea, heading toward the west, white, in groups, whose number no one knows except God, the Mighty and Majestic. When evening comes, the same number returns black." He said: "Did you notice this?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Those birds have in their crops the spirits of the people of Pharaoh, presented to the Fire morning and evening. Then they return to their nests, their feathers burned and turned black. Then white feathers grow on them at night, and the black ones fall out. Then they go out to the Fire morning and evening, then return to their nests. That is their state in this world. When the Day of Resurrection comes, God, Exalted, says: ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment﴾." He said: They used to say that they were six hundred thousand fighting men [Tafsir al-Tabari (24/46)].

Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq narrated to us, Malik informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar [In A: "Ibn Umar radiyallahu 'anhuma".] who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When any one of you dies, his seat (in the Hereafter) is shown to him morning and evening. If he is one of the people of Paradise, then (it is shown as) one of the people of Paradise; and if he is one of the people of the Fire, then (it is shown as) one of the people of the Fire. It is said to him: 'This is your seat, until Allah resurrects you on the Day of Resurrection.'"

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in their Sahihs through the narration of Malik, with the same chain [Al-Musnad (2/113), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1379), and Sahih Muslim no. (2866).].

Ibn Kathir said:

Allah, the Exalted, informs about the mutual disputes of the people of the Fire within the Fire, and Pharaoh and his people are among them. ﴿The weak will say﴾ (al-du'afa', i.e., the followers) ﴿to those who were arrogant﴾ (i.e., the leaders, the masters, and the great ones): ﴿Indeed, we were following you﴾ meaning, we obeyed you in what you called us to in the world of disbelief and misguidance. ﴿So will you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?﴾ meaning, a share that you would bear on our behalf.

﴿Those who were arrogant will say: Indeed, we are all in it﴾ meaning, we will not bear anything on your behalf; we have enough of our own, and of the punishment and torment we ourselves are suffering. ﴿Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants﴾ meaning, He is apportioning the punishment between us according to what each of us deserves, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿He will say, "For each is double, but you do not know"﴾ [al-A'raf: 38].

﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell: "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment."﴾ When they knew that Allah, the Exalted, does not respond to them nor listen to their supplication, but rather He has said: ﴿"Remain in it, and do not speak to Me"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 108], they asked the keepers (khazanah, the guardians of Hell, who are like the gatekeepers of the people of the Fire) that they should invoke Allah on their behalf to lighten the punishment for the disbelievers, even for one day. The keepers said to them, responding: ﴿"Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?"﴾ meaning, were not the proofs established against you in the world through the tongues of the messengers? ﴿They said: "Yes." They said: "Then invoke"﴾ meaning, you invoke for yourselves; we will not invoke on your behalf, nor will we listen to you, nor do we wish your deliverance, and we are free of you. Then we inform you that whether you invoke or do not invoke, it is the same: you will not be answered, and the punishment will not be lightened for you. For this reason they said: ﴿"And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error"﴾, meaning, only in loss, which will not be accepted and will not be answered.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 40, verses 51–56:

Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, raised a question regarding the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world﴾. He said: It is known that some of the Prophets, peace be upon them, were killed entirely by their people, such as Yahya, Zakariyya and Sha'ya', and some of them left among their people, either migrating, like Ibrahim (peace be upon him), or ascending to the sky, like 'Isa (peace be upon him). So where is the help in this world? He then answered this with two answers.

The first: the statement came in general terms, and what is meant is some of them. He said: This is permissible in the Arabic language.

The second: what is meant by help is avenging them against those who harmed them, whether that happened in their presence, in their absence, or after their deaths. This was done to the killers of Yahya, Zakariyya and Sha'ya'. Some of their enemies were empowered over them, humiliating them and shedding their blood. It is mentioned that Allah seized Nimrod with the seizure of the Mighty, the Powerful. As for those among the Jews who sought to crucify al-Masih (peace be upon him), Allah empowered the Romans over them, and they humiliated and disgraced them, and Allah made them victorious over them. Then, before the Day of Resurrection, 'Isa son of Maryam will descend as a just leader and an equitable judge. He will kill al-Masih al-Dajjal (the false messiah) and his Jewish soldiers, kill the pig, break the cross, and abolish the jizya (poll tax), so that only Islam will be accepted. This is a great victory. This is the custom of Allah with His creation, in ancient and recent times: He helps His believing servants in this world and comforts their eyes against those who harmed them. In Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Allah, the Exalted, says: Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him." And in another hadith: "Indeed, I avenge My friends just as the lion avenges, the fierce one." I have not found this wording; Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilya (1/11) as a statement attributed to Ibn 'Abbas: "And I am the avenger of My friends on the Day of Resurrection."

For this reason, Allah, the Exalted, destroyed the people of Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of al-Rass, the people of Lut, and the people of Madyan, and their likes and counterparts, from among those who denied the messengers and opposed the truth. Allah saved the believers from among them, so He did not destroy any of them, and He punished the disbelievers, so none of them escaped.

Al-Suddi said: Allah never sent a messenger to a people who killed him, or to a group of believers calling to the truth who were killed, without that generation passing away until Allah raised for them someone who would support them and seek vengeance for their blood from those who did this to them in this world. He said: So the Prophets and the believers were killed in this world, yet they were victorious in it.

Thus Allah, [glorified is He], helped His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions against those who opposed him, opposed him, denied him and showed enmity to him. He made His word supreme and His religion prevail over all other religions. He commanded him to migrate from among his people to the City of the Prophet (Madinah), and made for him there helpers and supporters. Then He granted him victory over the polytheists at the Battle of Badr, giving him victory over them and defeating them for his sake. He killed their chieftains, captured their nobles, and led them away bound in shackles. Then he showed them favour by accepting ransom from them. Then, after a short period, He gave him (ﷺ) the conquest of Makkah, and his eyes were comforted in his homeland, the sacred, inviolable, honoured and exalted city. Allah rescued through him its people from what they were in of shirk and disbelief. He opened Yemen for him, and the whole Arabian Peninsula submitted to him, and people entered the religion of Allah in multitudes. Then Allah took him to Himself, because of the great honour he had with Him. Then Allah established his Companions as successors after him, and they conveyed the religion of Allah from him and called the servants of Allah to Allah. They opened the lands, the districts, the regions, the cities, the towns, the villages and the hearts, until the Muhammadan call spread across the eastern and western parts of the earth. This religion will continue to stand, victorious and dominant, until the Hour is established. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection the help will be greater, mightier and more glorious.

Mujahid said: "The witnesses" (al-ashhad) are the angels.

* *

His words: ﴿The Day when their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers﴾ are a substitute (badal) for His words: ﴿and the Day when the witnesses stand﴾.

Others recited: "yawmu" with a nominative vowel (raf'), as if He explained it with it: ﴿and the Day when the witnesses stand, the Day when their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers﴾. The wrongdoers are the polytheists. ﴿Their excuses﴾ means no excuse or ransom will be accepted from them. ﴿And for them is the curse﴾, meaning distance and expulsion from mercy. ﴿And for them is the evil abode﴾, which is the Fire. This was said by al-Suddi: "an evil dwelling and resting place."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And for them is the evil abode﴾, meaning the evil outcome.

* *

His words: ﴿And We had certainly given Musa the guidance﴾, which is what Allah sent him with of guidance and light. ﴿And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture﴾, meaning We made the final outcome theirs, and We made them inherit the lands, wealth, treasures and territory of Fir'awn, because they were patient in obeying Allah and following His messenger Musa (peace be upon him). And in the Scripture that they inherited, which is the Torah, ﴿is guidance and a reminder for people of understanding﴾, meaning sound and upright intellects.

* *

His words: ﴿So be patient﴾, meaning: O Muhammad. ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah﴾, meaning: We promised you that We would exalt your word and make the final outcome yours and that of those who follow you, and Allah does not fail in His promise. What We have informed you of is true, without any doubt or uncertainty.

* *

His words: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. This is an incitement of the Ummah to seek forgiveness. ﴿And exalt the praise of your Lord in the evening﴾, meaning at the ends of the day and the beginnings of the night, ﴿and in the morning﴾, which are the beginnings of the day and the ends of the night.

* *

His words: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having come to them﴾, meaning they repel the truth with falsehood and reject the sound proofs with corrupt doubts, without any evidence or proof from Allah. ﴿There is nothing in their breasts but pride, which they will never attain﴾.

Meaning: there is nothing in their breasts but arrogance toward following the truth and contempt for the one who brought it to them. What they aim at, namely obscuring the truth and raising falsehood, will not be achieved by them. Rather, the truth is what is elevated, and their words and intentions are what is cast down. ﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾, meaning from the condition of such people. ﴿Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾. Or (it means): from the evil of such disputants concerning the signs of Allah without authority. This is the tafsir of Ibn Jarir.

Ka'b and Abu al-'Aliyah said: This verse was revealed concerning the Jews: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having come to them; there is nothing in their breasts but pride, which they will never attain﴾. Abu al-'Aliyah said: That is because they claimed that the Dajjal would be from among them, and that through him they would rule the earth. So Allah said to His Prophet (ﷺ), commanding him to seek refuge from the trial of the Dajjal, and for this reason He said: ﴿So seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾.

This is a strange statement, and it contains far-fetched interpretation, although Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his book. And Allah knows best.

His words: ﴿So be patient﴾, meaning: O Muhammad. ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah﴾, meaning: We promised you that We would exalt your word and make the final outcome yours and that of those who follow you, and Allah does not fail in His promise. What We have informed you of is true, without any doubt or uncertainty.

* *

His words: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. This is an incitement of the Ummah to seek forgiveness. ﴿And exalt the praise of your Lord in the evening﴾, meaning at the ends of the day and the beginnings of the night, ﴿and in the morning﴾, which are the beginnings of the day and the ends of the night.

* *

His words: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having come to them﴾, meaning they repel the truth with falsehood and reject the sound proofs with corrupt doubts, without any evidence or proof from Allah. ﴿There is nothing in their breasts but pride, which they will never attain﴾.

Meaning: there is nothing in their breasts but arrogance toward following the truth and contempt for the one who brought it to them. What they aim at, namely obscuring the truth and raising falsehood, will not be achieved by them. Rather, the truth is what is elevated, and their words and intentions are what is cast down. ﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾, meaning from the condition of such people. ﴿Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾. Or (it means): from the evil of such disputants concerning the signs of Allah without authority. This is the tafsir of Ibn Jarir.

Ka'b and Abu al-'Aliyah said: This verse was revealed concerning the Jews: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having come to them; there is nothing in their breasts but pride, which they will never attain﴾. Abu al-'Aliyah said: That is because they claimed that the Dajjal would be from among them, and that through him they would rule the earth. So Allah said to His Prophet (ﷺ), commanding him to seek refuge from the trial of the Dajjal, and for this reason He said: ﴿So seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾.

This is a strange statement, and it contains far-fetched interpretation, although Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his book. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 40, verses 51–56:

Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, raised a question regarding the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world﴾. He said: It is known that some of the Prophets, peace be upon them, were killed entirely by their people, such as Yahya, Zakariyya and Sha'ya', and some of them left among their people, either migrating, like Ibrahim (peace be upon him), or ascending to the sky, like 'Isa (peace be upon him). So where is the help in this world? He then answered this with two answers.

The first: the statement came in general terms, and what is meant is some of them. He said: This is permissible in the Arabic language.

The second: what is meant by help is avenging them against those who harmed them, whether that happened in their presence, in their absence, or after their deaths. This was done to the killers of Yahya, Zakariyya and Sha'ya'. Some of their enemies were empowered over them, humiliating them and shedding their blood. It is mentioned that Allah seized Nimrod with the seizure of the Mighty, the Powerful. As for those among the Jews who sought to crucify al-Masih (peace be upon him), Allah empowered the Romans over them, and they humiliated and disgraced them, and Allah made them victorious over them. Then, before the Day of Resurrection, 'Isa son of Maryam will descend as a just leader and an equitable judge. He will kill al-Masih al-Dajjal (the false messiah) and his Jewish soldiers, kill the pig, break the cross, and abolish the jizya (poll tax), so that only Islam will be accepted. This is a great victory. This is the custom of Allah with His creation, in ancient and recent times: He helps His believing servants in this world and comforts their eyes against those who harmed them. In Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Allah, the Exalted, says: Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him." And in another hadith: "Indeed, I avenge My friends just as the lion avenges, the fierce one." I have not found this wording; Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilya (1/11) as a statement attributed to Ibn 'Abbas: "And I am the avenger of My friends on the Day of Resurrection."

For this reason, Allah, the Exalted, destroyed the people of Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of al-Rass, the people of Lut, and the people of Madyan, and their likes and counterparts, from among those who denied the messengers and opposed the truth. Allah saved the believers from among them, so He did not destroy any of them, and He punished the disbelievers, so none of them escaped.

Al-Suddi said: Allah never sent a messenger to a people who killed him, or to a group of believers calling to the truth who were killed, without that generation passing away until Allah raised for them someone who would support them and seek vengeance for their blood from those who did this to them in this world. He said: So the Prophets and the believers were killed in this world, yet they were victorious in it.

Thus Allah, [glorified is He], helped His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions against those who opposed him, opposed him, denied him and showed enmity to him. He made His word supreme and His religion prevail over all other religions. He commanded him to migrate from among his people to the City of the Prophet (Madinah), and made for him there helpers and supporters. Then He granted him victory over the polytheists at the Battle of Badr, giving him victory over them and defeating them for his sake. He killed their chieftains, captured their nobles, and led them away bound in shackles. Then he showed them favour by accepting ransom from them. Then, after a short period, He gave him (ﷺ) the conquest of Makkah, and his eyes were comforted in his homeland, the sacred, inviolable, honoured and exalted city. Allah rescued through him its people from what they were in of shirk and disbelief. He opened Yemen for him, and the whole Arabian Peninsula submitted to him, and people entered the religion of Allah in multitudes. Then Allah took him to Himself, because of the great honour he had with Him. Then Allah established his Companions as successors after him, and they conveyed the religion of Allah from him and called the servants of Allah to Allah. They opened the lands, the districts, the regions, the cities, the towns, the villages and the hearts, until the Muhammadan call spread across the eastern and western parts of the earth. This religion will continue to stand, victorious and dominant, until the Hour is established. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection the help will be greater, mightier and more glorious.

Mujahid said: "The witnesses" (al-ashhad) are the angels.

* *

His words: ﴿The Day when their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers﴾ are a substitute (badal) for His words: ﴿and the Day when the witnesses stand﴾.

Others recited: "yawmu" with a nominative vowel (raf'), as if He explained it with it: ﴿and the Day when the witnesses stand, the Day when their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers﴾. The wrongdoers are the polytheists. ﴿Their excuses﴾ means no excuse or ransom will be accepted from them. ﴿And for them is the curse﴾, meaning distance and expulsion from mercy. ﴿And for them is the evil abode﴾, which is the Fire. This was said by al-Suddi: "an evil dwelling and resting place."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And for them is the evil abode﴾, meaning the evil outcome.

* *

His words: ﴿And We had certainly given Musa the guidance﴾, which is what Allah sent him with of guidance and light. ﴿And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture﴾, meaning We made the final outcome theirs, and We made them inherit the lands, wealth, treasures and territory of Fir'awn, because they were patient in obeying Allah and following His messenger Musa (peace be upon him). And in the Scripture that they inherited, which is the Torah, ﴿is guidance and a reminder for people of understanding﴾, meaning sound and upright intellects.

* *

His words: ﴿So be patient﴾, meaning: O Muhammad. ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah﴾, meaning: We promised you that We would exalt your word and make the final outcome yours and that of those who follow you, and Allah does not fail in His promise. What We have informed you of is true, without any doubt or uncertainty.

* *

* *

Ibn Kathir said: He, may He be exalted, says, drawing attention to the fact that He will resurrect the creatures on the Day of Resurrection, and that this is easy for Him and effortless in His sight, by [pointing to] the fact that He created the heavens and the earth, and the creation of them both is greater than the creation of mankind, in origination and in restoration. Whoever is able to do that is able to do what is less than it all the more, by way of priority and greater fitness, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed He is Competent over all things.﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 33] [[In manuscripts T and A: "Or is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed He is Competent over all things," which is an error; the correct reading is what we have established, since the scribes of the two manuscripts T and A confused the eighty-first verse of Surah Ya-Sin with the thirty-third verse of Surah al-Ahqaf.]]. And here He said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know.﴾ So for this reason they do not reflect upon this proof nor contemplate it, just as many of the Arabs acknowledged that Allah created the heavens and the earth, yet denied the Return out of disbelief, obstinacy and stubbornness. And they had acknowledged what is more fitting than what they denied.

Then He said: ﴿And the blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer.﴾ That is, just as the blind man who sees nothing is not equal to the seeing man who sees whatever his sight reaches, rather there is a great difference between them, so likewise the believing righteous are not equal to the disbelieving wicked. ﴿Little do you remember﴾, that is: how little do many people remember.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, the Hour is surely coming﴾ [[In T: "āti'ah" (coming), which is an error.]], that is, it will certainly occur and come to pass, ﴿there is no doubt about it, but most of mankind do not believe﴾, that is, they do not affirm it, rather they deny its existence.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to us, Ashhab narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, from an elderly Shaykh from the people of Yemen, who had come from there, who said: I heard that when the Hour draws near, trials intensify upon the people, and the heat of the sun intensifies.

Ibn Kathir said: He, may He be exalted, says, drawing attention to the fact that He will resurrect the creatures on the Day of Resurrection, and that this is easy for Him and effortless in His sight, by [pointing to] the fact that He created the heavens and the earth, and the creation of them both is greater than the creation of mankind, in origination and in restoration. This is part of His grace and generosity, may He be blessed and exalted, that He urged His servants to call upon Him and guaranteed them a response, just as Sufyan al-Thawri used to say: "O You, whose servant is most beloved to You is the one who asks You and asks You often, and O You, whose servant is most hateful to You is the one who does not ask You, and there is none like that other than You, O Lord."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

On this same meaning, the poet says:

Allah becomes angry if you abandon asking Him,
while the son of Adam becomes angry when he is asked.

Qatadah said: Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "This Ummah was given three things that no nation before them was given, except a prophet: when Allah sent a prophet, it was said to him, 'You are a witness over your nation,' and [Allah said to this Ummah], 'We have made you witnesses over mankind.' It was said to him, 'There is no hardship for you in the religion,' and He said to this Ummah, ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ [al-Hajj 22:78]. It was said to him, 'Call upon Me, and I will respond to you,' and He said to this Ummah, ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Al-Imam al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Muthanna al-Mawsili said in his Musnad (a collection of hadith arranged by the narrators' names): Abu Ibrahim al-Turjumani narrated to us, Salih al-Murri narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Hasan narrating from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, in what he relates from his Lord, mighty and majestic, that he said: "There are four qualities: one of them is for Me, one for you, one between Me and you, and one between you and My servants. As for the one for Me, you worship Me and do not associate anything with Me. As for the one for you, whatever good you do, I will reward you for it. As for the one between Me and you, from you is the supplication and upon Me is the response. As for the one between you and My servants, you should be content for them with what you are content for yourself."

[[Musnad Abi Ya'la (5/143). Al-Bazzar also narrated it in his Musnad, no. (19) in Kashf al-Astar, through al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal from Salih al-Murri with the same chain, and he said: "Salih al-Murri alone narrated it." Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/51): "Its chain includes Salih al-Murri, who is weak, and the tadlis (concealment of defects in a chain) of al-Hasan as well. The intended one here is Salih ibn Bashir al-Murri, who is extremely weak, and he alone narrated it."]]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Dharr, from Yusay' al-Kindi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, supplication is worship." Then he recited: ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled﴾.

It was narrated in this manner by the compilers of the Sunan (collections of hadith arranged by legal topics): al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Jarir, all from the hadith of al-A'mash, with this chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

[[Musnad (4/271), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3372), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11464), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3828), and Tafsir al-Tabari (24/51).]]

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and also Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Shu'ba, from Mansur, from Dharr, with this chain. Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Mansur and al-A'mash, both from Dharr, with this chain.

[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1479), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2969), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11446), and Tafsir al-Tabari (24/51). Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it, no. (3247).]]

Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim narrated it in their two Sahihs, and al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sahih."

[[Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (2396), Mawarid edition, and al-Mustadrak (1/491).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Abu Malih al-Madani narrated to me, a shaykh from the people of Madinah, who heard it from Abu Salih, and at another time he said: I heard Abu Salih narrating from Abu Hurayra [may Allah be pleased with him] who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever does not call upon Allah, mighty and majestic, He will be angry with him."

Ahmad alone narrated it with this wording, and this is a chain with no problem.

[[Musnad (2/477). Ahmad alone narrated it with this wording; otherwise Ibn Majah narrated it in al-Sunan no. (3827) through Waki' with this chain, with the wording: "Whoever does not ask Allah, He will be angry with him."]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Marwan al-Fazari narrated to us, Sabih Abu al-Malih narrated to us: I heard Abu Salih narrating from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever does not ask Him, He will be angry with him."

[[Musnad (2/442).]]

Ibn Ma'in said: This Abu al-Malih's name is Sabih, with a damma (short u vowel) on the sabad, as Abd al-Ghani ibn Sa'id specified. As for this Abu Salih, he is al-Khuzi, who settled in Shi'b al-Khuz. This was said by al-Bazzar in his Musnad. Similarly, in his narration there occurs Abu al-Malih al-Farisi, from Abu Salih al-Khuzi, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever does not ask Allah, He will be angry with him."

[[Also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (3373), and he said: "Abu al-Malih's name is Sabih, and I heard Muhammad (al-Bukhari) say this, and he said that he was Persian (fariси)."]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ramahurmuzi said: Hammam narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, Na'il ibn Najih narrated to us, Ca'idh ibn Habib narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id, who said: When Muhammad ibn Maslama al-Ansari died, we found in the tassel of his sword a writing: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Indeed, your Lord has breezes (nafahat) in the remainder of your time, so expose yourselves to them, for perhaps a supplication will coincide with a mercy, and by it its owner will be made happy with a happiness after which he never loses.'"

[[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (19/233) through another route.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me﴾, meaning: to call upon Me and to affirm My oneness, ﴿will enter Hell, humbled﴾, meaning: abased and despised, as Imam Ahmad said:

Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ibn Ajlan, Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The arrogant will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in the forms of men, resembling ants, while everything abases them, until they enter a prison in Hell called Bulas. Fire of the fires will overwhelm them, and they will be given to drink from the clay of the defilement (tinat al-khabal), the pus of the people of the Fire."

[[Musnad (2/179).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunays narrated to us: I heard my father narrating from Wuhayb ibn al-Ward: A man narrated to me, who said: "I was walking one day in the land of the Romans, when I heard a caller from atop a mountain peak saying: 'O Lord, I am amazed at the one who knows You, how he could hope for anyone other than You! O Lord, I am amazed at the one who knows You, how he could seek his needs from anyone other than You!'" He said: "Then I left, and then the great calamity came." He said: "Then it returned a second time, saying: 'O Lord, I am amazed at the one who knows You, how he could expose himself to anything of Your wrath that pleases other than You.'" Wuhayb said: "This is the great calamity." He said: "I called out to him: 'Are you a jinn or a human?' He said: 'Rather, a human. Occupy yourself with what concerns you, away from what does not concern you.'"

He, exalted is He, says, reminding His creation of the favour He has bestowed on them by making the night for them, in which they rest and find relief from the constant movement of their pursuit of livelihood by day, and by making the day bright, that is, illuminated, so that they can move about in it for travel, crossing regions, and engaging in trades and crafts. ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty towards mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks﴾ [[In manuscript T: "but most of them." This is an error.]] meaning: they do not fulfil the duty of thanking Allah for the blessings He has bestowed upon them.

Then He said: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no god but Him﴾. That is, the One who did these things is Allah, the One, the Unique, the Creator of things, besides whom there is no god and no lord. ﴿How then are you deluded?﴾ That is, how can you worship other than Him, such as idols, which create nothing, but are themselves created and carved.

* *

His saying: ﴿Thus are deluded those who used to deny the signs of Allah﴾. That is, just as these people went astray by worshipping other than Allah, so too were those before them deluded, worshipping other than Him without any proof or evidence, but merely out of ignorance and desire, and they denied the proofs and signs of Allah.

* *

His saying: ﴿Allah is He who made the earth a place of rest for you﴾. That is, He made it a settled place for you, a spread-out and cradle-like expanse on which you live, act and walk along its broad paths, and He fixed it firm with mountains so that it would not shake with you. ﴿And the sky as a canopy﴾, that is, a protected roof over the world. ﴿And He shaped you and perfected your forms﴾, that is, He created you in the most excellent shapes and granted you the most complete forms in the finest proportion. ﴿And provided you with good things﴾, that is, with food and drink in this world. Thus He mentioned that He created the abode, the inhabitants and the provisions. He is the Creator and the Provider, as He said in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, so that you may be mindful. Who made the earth a bed for you and the sky a canopy, and sent down water from the sky and thereby brought forth fruits as provision for you. So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21–22]. Allah the Exalted says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: Indeed Allah forbids that anyone other than Him be worshipped, whether idols, rivals, or images. Allah the Exalted has made clear that none deserves worship besides Him, in His saying: ﴿He it is who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then He brings you out as a child, then [He lets you reach your maturity] and then [He lets you become] old men﴾. That is, He is the One who turns you through all these stages, alone, with no partner, and all of that occurs by His command, His arrangement and His decree.

﴿And among you is one who is taken in death before﴾, that is, before he is brought into existence and comes out into this world; rather, his mother miscarries him. Among them also is one who dies as a child, as a youth, or as a middle-aged man before reaching old age, as in His saying: ﴿So that We may make clear to you. And We cause to remain in the wombs what We will for a specified term﴾ [Al-Hajj: 5]. And He said here: ﴿so that you may understand﴾. Ibn Juraij said: that you may remember the Resurrection.

Then He said: ﴿He it is who gives life and causes death﴾, that is, He alone is characterized by this; none other than Him is able to do this. ﴿And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾, that is, it is not opposed, nor is it prevented; rather, whatever He wills comes to be [without doubt] [[Addition from manuscripts S and A.]].

Allah says: Do you not marvel, O Muhammad, at these deniers of Allah's signs, who dispute about truth and falsehood? How their minds are turned away from guidance to misguidance. ﴿Those who deny the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers﴾, i.e., of guidance and clarification, ﴿but they will come to know﴾. This is a severe threat and a firm warning from the Lord, exalted is His majesty, to these people, as He says: ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾ [al-Mursalat: 15].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿When the shackles are around their necks, and the chains﴾, i.e., connected to the shackles, in the hands of the Zabaniyah (the angels of punishment), who drag them on their faces, sometimes to the boiling water (hamim) and sometimes to the Hellfire (jahim). Therefore He says: ﴿They will be dragged through scalding water; then in the Fire they will be set ablaze﴾. As He says: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals denied. They will circulate between it and scalding water, intensely hot﴾ [ar-Rahman: 43-44]. And after mentioning their eating of the zaqqum and their drinking of boiling water, He said: ﴿Then indeed their return is to the Hellfire﴾ [as-Saffat: 68], and He said: ﴿And the companions of the left, what are the companions of the left? In scorching wind and scalding water, and a shade of black smoke, neither cool nor pleasant﴾, until He said: ﴿Then indeed you, O astray deniers, will be eating from a tree of zaqqum, filling your bellies with it, and drinking on top of it from scalding water, drinking like thirsty camels. This is their hospitality on the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 41-56]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the sinner, like murky oil, boiling in the bellies like the boiling of scalding water. Seize him and drag him into the midst of Hellfire. Then pour over his head the torment of scalding water. Taste it; indeed you were the mighty, the noble. This is what you used to doubt﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 43-50]. That is, it is said to them this in a manner of rebuke, reproach, belittling, humiliation, mockery and ridicule.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to us, Mansur ibn Ammar narrated to us, Bishr [in A: "Bishr"] ibn Talhah al-Khizami narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Duraik, from Ya'la ibn Munyah, (his narration raised to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ), who said: "Allah will create a cloud for the people of the Fire, black and dark, and it will be said: 'O people of the Fire, what do you seek?' They will remember the clouds of the world and say: 'We ask for the coolness of drink.' So it will rain upon them shackles that increase their shackles, chains that increase their chains, and embers that ignite the Fire upon them." This is a gharib hadith [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat, no. (4846), and Ibn Adi in al-Kamil (6/394) via Ahmad ibn Mani' from Mansur with it. Al-Tabarani said: "It is not narrated except through this chain; Mansur alone transmitted it." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/390): "In it is one who is slightly weak, and in it is one I do not know."].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then it will be said to them: Where is that which you used to associate with Allah?﴾, i.e., it will be said to them: Where are the idols that you used to worship besides Allah? Can they help you today? ﴿They will say: They have departed from us﴾, i.e., they have gone and did not benefit us, ﴿Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before﴾, i.e., they denied their worship, as in His saying: ﴿Then their response will be only that they say: By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23]. Therefore He says: ﴿Thus does Allah lead astray the disbelievers﴾.

* *

And wretched is the residence of the arrogant﴾, i.e., wretched is the abode and place of rest, in which is humiliation and severe punishment, for those who were arrogant toward the signs of Allah and toward following His proofs and evidences.

They will remember the clouds of the world and say: 'We ask for the coolness of drink.' So it will rain upon them shackles that increase their shackles, chains that increase their chains, and embers that ignite the Fire upon them." This is a gharib hadith [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat, no. (4846), and Ibn Adi in al-Kamil (6/394) via Ahmad ibn Mani' from Mansur with it. Al-Tabarani said: "It is not narrated except through this chain; Mansur alone transmitted it." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/390): "In it is one who is slightly weak, and in it is one I do not know."].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then it will be said to them: Where is that which you used to associate with Allah?﴾, i.e., it will be said to them: Where are the idols that you used to worship besides Allah? Can they help you today? ﴿They will say: They have departed from us﴾, i.e., they have gone and did not benefit us, ﴿Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before﴾, i.e., they denied their worship, as in His saying: ﴿Then their response will be only that they say: By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23]. Therefore He says: ﴿Thus does Allah lead astray the disbelievers﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿That is because you used to rejoice in the earth without right and because you used to exult﴾, i.e., the angels will say to them: This which you are in is a recompense for your rejoicing in the world without right, your exultation, your insolence and your arrogance. ﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein. And wretched is the residence of the arrogant﴾, i.e., wretched is the abode and place of rest, in which is humiliation and severe punishment, for those who were arrogant toward the signs of Allah and toward following His proofs and evidences.

Allah, exalted is He, says, instructing His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to be patient over the denial of those among his people who denied him. Indeed, Allah will fulfill for you what He promised you of victory and triumph over your people, and He made the final outcome yours and that of those who follow you, in this world and in the Hereafter. ﴿So whether We show you some of what We promise them﴾ means: in this world. And so it happened: Allah gladdened their eyes (the eyes of the believers) by [destroying] their great ones and their leaders, who were annihilated on the Day of Badr. Then Allah granted him the conquest of Makkah and the rest of the Arabian Peninsula during his lifetime, peace and blessings be upon him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿or We take you [in death], then to Us they will be returned﴾, it means: then We will make them taste the severe punishment in the Hereafter.

Then He said, consoling him: ﴿And We had already sent messengers before you; among them are those We have related to you and among them are those We have not related to you﴾, just as He said in Surat an-Nisa' exactly. That is: among them are those whose news and stories with their peoples We have revealed to you, how their peoples denied them, and then the outcome and victory were for the messengers. ﴿And among them are those We have not related to you﴾, and they are far more numerous than those mentioned, by multiples of multiples, as has already been pointed out in Surat an-Nisa' [[See the commentary on verse 164 of Surat an-Nisa'.]]. And to Allah belong all praise and favor.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah﴾, it means: no messenger was able to bring his people something that breaks the customary order, except that Allah permitted him to do so; and this indicates his truthfulness in what he brought them. ﴿So when the command of Allah comes﴾, which is His punishment and retribution encompassing the deniers, ﴿it will be concluded in truth﴾, so the believers will be saved and the disbelievers will perish. For this reason He said: ﴿And there the falsifiers will lose﴾.

He, exalted is He, reminds His servants of the favours He has bestowed upon them through the livestock (al-an'am) He created for them, namely camels, cattle and sheep: ﴿Of them they have their mounts, and of them they eat﴾ [Yasin: 72]. Camels are ridden, eaten and milked, and loads are carried on them on journeys and in travel baggage to distant lands and far-off regions. Cattle are eaten, their milk is drunk, and the land is ploughed with them. Sheep are eaten and their milk is drunk. From all of them, their wool, hair and fleece are shorn, and from these are made furnishings, clothing and goods, as Allah explained and clarified in places mentioned earlier in "Surah al-An'am" [[See the commentary on verses 141-144 of Surah al-An'am.]], "Surah al-Nahl" [[See the commentary on verses 5-8 of Surah al-Nahl.]], and elsewhere. For this reason He says here: ﴿That you may ride upon some of them and of them you eat. And for you in them are benefits, and that you may reach upon them a need within your breasts, and upon them and upon the ship you are carried.﴾

* *

His words ﴿And He shows you His signs﴾ mean: His proofs and evidences in the horizons and within yourselves. ﴿So which of Allah's signs will you deny?﴾ means: you are not able to deny any of His signs, except by obstinately opposing and arrogantly rejecting them.

His words ﴿And He shows you His signs﴾ mean: His proofs and evidences in the horizons and within yourselves. ﴿So which of Allah's signs will you deny?﴾ means: you are not able to deny any of His signs, except by obstinately opposing and arrogantly rejecting them.

﴿Allah the Exalted informs about the nations that denied the messengers in ancient times, and what severe punishment befell them despite their great strength, and what they had left behind on the earth and the wealth they had amassed. None of that availed them anything, nor did it repel from them an atom of the might of Allah.﴾ That was because, when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, decisive arguments and conclusive evidence, they paid them no heed and did not accept them. They were content with the knowledge they had, in their own opinion, and disdained what the messengers had brought them.

Mujahid said: They said, "We are more knowledgeable than them. We will not be resurrected, nor will we be punished."

Al-Suddi said: They rejoiced in the knowledge they had, out of their ignorance, so there came upon them from the might of Allah what they had no power to withstand.

﴿And there encompassed them﴾, that is, surrounded them, ﴿what they used to mock﴾, that is, what they used to deny and consider impossible to occur.

﴿So when they saw Our might﴾, that is, they witnessed the punishment falling upon them, ﴿they said, "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ That is, they declared Allah to be One and rejected the false deities (al-Taghut). But this came at a time when stumbling is no longer accepted and excuses no longer benefit. This is like what Pharaoh said when drowning overtook him: ﴿I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims﴾ [Yunus: 90]. Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters﴾ [Yunus: 91]. That is, Allah did not accept it from him, because He had answered the supplication of His Prophet Musa against him when he said: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 88].

And here too He said: ﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might. This is the way of Allah which has passed among His servants.﴾ That is, this is the ruling of Allah regarding all who repent at the moment of witnessing the punishment: it is not accepted. For this reason there came in the hadith: "Indeed, Allah accepts the repentance of the servant so long as he has not begun to gasp (yugharghir)." That is, once he gasps and the soul reaches the throat and he sees the angel, there is no repentance at that time. For this reason He said: ﴿And there the disbelievers will be lost.﴾

The end of the tafsir of "Surah Ghafir" [in S: "al-Mu'min"]. And to Allah belongs all praise and grace.
